summary: Franz-Karl Ehrhard worked in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. Educated at the University of Hamburg under Lambert Schmithausen, he was Resident Representative for the Nepal Research Centre (1988–1993) and Professor at the University of Munich (2001–2019).
François Grimal is an Indologist. He held a post at the École Pratique des Hautes Études and served as Director of the École française d'Extrême-Orient (attested 2003).
François Gros was an Indologist who studied at the University of Lyon and under Pierre Meile and Jean Filliozat. He served as Directeur d'études at the École Pratique des Hautes Études (~1977–2002).
François Lachaud is a scholar of Japanology, Buddhist studies, and Sinology. He held a post at the École française d'Extrême-Orient, where he is attested as Professor in 2008.

François Martini was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Sylvain Lévi and at INALCO. He served at INALCO (Professor from 1928), the Buddhist Institute (General Secretary, ~1936–1944), and the École Pratique des Hautes Études (~1957–1965).
François-Marie Bertrand was an Indologist who studied at the Séminaire de Saint-Sulpice and under Garcin de Tassy.

Françoise L'Hernault was an Indologist and archaeologist who studied at INALCO, Annamalai University, and Sorbonne Nouvelle University. In 1971, she joined the École française d'Extrême-Orient in charge of photographic collections.

Françoise Mallison is an Indology and religious studies scholar who studied under Charlotte Vaudeville. In 1988, she succeeded Vaudeville as Directeur d'Études at the École Pratique des Hautes Études.

Françoise Pommaret is a Tibetologist and historian educated at INALCO, the Sorbonne, and the University of Paris. She served as Director of Langues et cultures de l'aire tibétaine and Directeur de recherche at the CNRS (from 2002).

Françoise Robin is a Tibetologist who earned her degrees at INALCO under Heather Stoddard. She served as Director at Collège de France (2009–2015) and held departmental headships at INALCO in 2011 and 2013–2014.

Fred Henry Andrews worked in archaeology and Iranian/Central Asian studies. He served as Curator of the Lahore Museum (~1890–1899), Director of the Art Department at Battersea Polytechnic Institute (~1899–1910), and Principal of Sri Pratap Technical College (1914).

Fred Pfeil was a scholar of Buddhist studies and other fields. He earned degrees from Amherst College and Stanford University, later teaching at Stanford, Stephens College, Oregon State University, and Trinity College, Hartford (~1983–2005).

Fred Walter Householder, Jr. was a linguist and Indologist who studied at the University of Vermont and Columbia University under Louis H. Gray. He lectured at Columbia and Allegheny College before joining Indiana University Bloomington (1948–1983).
Freda Bedi was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology figure who studied at St Hugh's College and under Mahasi Sayadaw. She founded the Young Lamas Home School and Karma Drubgyu Thargay Ling Nunnery.

Frede Møller-Kristensen was an Indologist who studied at the University of Copenhagen, where he was a lecturer in Pāli (1966–1972). He also served as Director of the Oriental Department at the Royal Danish Library (1969–1987).

Frederic Salmon Growse was an Indologist and archaeologist who studied at Oriel College and The Queen's College, Oxford. He served in the Indian Civil Service (~1860–1891) and was a Fellow of the University of Calcutta.
Frederic Spring was an Indologist and linguist who served as a missionary for the Church Mission Society and as a Chaplain in the Madras Army until 1824.

Frederick Eden Pargiter was an Indologist educated at Exeter College. He served in the Indian Civil Service (~1875–1904), was a Calcutta High Court Judge (1904–1906), and was President of The Asiatic Society (1903–1905).

Frederick J. Streng was a scholar of Buddhist studies, religion, and philosophy. Educated at SMU, Banaras Hindu University, and the University of Chicago under Mircea Eliade, he taught at USC (1963–1966) and SMU (1966–1974).

Frederick James Furnivall was a linguist educated at UCL and Trinity Hall. He served as Secretary of the Philological Society (1853–1910), editor of the Oxford English Dictionary (1861–1870), and taught at the Working Men's College (~1854–1910).
